newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: NOL says liner freight rates stabilising.
newsitem.headline: NOL says liner freight rates stabilising.

text.p: Shipping group Neptune Orient Lines Ltd (NOL) believes liner freight rates have stabilised, chief executive officer Lua Cheng Eng said on Monday.
Lua told reporters that keen competition in liner rates had hit the group's results in the six months ended June 30 1996.
He said NOL's net profit dived 43 percent to Singapore $10.18 million, turnover was a flat S$937.15 million and operating pre-tax profit was down 61 percent to S$6.48 million.

If it had not been for $17.1 million in profits from the sale of vessels, the group would have made an operating loss with turnover flat despite better liftings and a stable Singapore dollar because liner rates were very weak, he said.

Liner trade accounts for about 80 percent of NOL's revenues. Lua said the recent merger between Britain's P&O and the Dutch Nedlloyd Group, was a positive development in the industry as it could lead to "some consolidation in the future and liner rates should stabilise".
NOL has a global partnership with P&O Containers to share resources and co-operate in land-based support activities.
Lua said he did not expect liner rates to go into "free fall as rates at that level are not going to do anybody any good".
He also said NOL was going ahead with Mitsui & Co to develop and operate a container terminal in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.
The terminal will be built in three phases with the first phase costing US$50 million.
